aiPolicyMetaDescription: Read how Digitaltableteur uses AI-assisted tools, the safeguards we apply, and your rights under EU law.
aiPolicyIntro: Digitaltableteur uses AI-assisted tools to enhance our design and development services while maintaining human oversight and accountability. We are committed to transparency about AI usage and compliance with the EU AI Act, GDPR, and emerging AI governance standards. This statement explains how, when, and why we use AI, the safeguards we implement, and your rights.
aiPolicyPrincipleHuman: Human accountability – Every AI-generated output is reviewed, validated, and approved by a qualified team member before delivery or publication.
aiPolicyPrincipleTransparency: Transparency – We document which AI tools are used in each project and disclose this to clients upon request.
aiPolicyPrinciplePrivacy: Privacy first – Personal data is minimized, anonymized, or excluded from AI prompts. We opt out of provider training programs.
aiPolicyPrincipleQuality: Quality assurance – AI is used as an assistive tool, not a replacement for professional expertise and judgment.
aiPolicyUseCaseDesign: Design exploration – generating alternative layouts, color palettes, or visual concepts for internal review. All AI suggestions are evaluated and refined by experienced designers before implementation.
aiPolicyUseCaseContent: Editorial assistance – drafting article outlines, alt text descriptions, meta descriptions, or translation suggestions. All content is fact-checked, edited for accuracy, and approved by a human editor.
aiPolicyUseCaseCode: Code assistance – generating code snippets, documentation, or refactoring suggestions using GitHub Copilot or similar tools. All code is reviewed, tested, and validated before deployment.
aiPolicyUseCaseOperations: Quality assurance – analyzing anonymized support tickets, error logs, and telemetry data to identify accessibility issues, performance bottlenecks, or user experience improvements.
aiPolicyUseCaseChat: Website chat – our chat widget uses OpenAI's API to answer visitor questions. Conversations are not stored for training purposes and are retained only as long as necessary.
aiPolicyNotUsedBody: We do not use AI for: automated decision-making that affects your rights; high-risk applications as defined by the EU AI Act; final design deliverables without human review; legal, financial, or medical advice; or making hiring or business decisions about individuals.
aiPolicyProvidersIntro: We work with the following AI service providers, all of which have data processing agreements and GDPR compliance measures:
aiPolicyProviderOpenAI: OpenAI (ChatGPT, GPT-4) – for chat functionality, content drafting, and code assistance. Data is not used for model training under our enterprise agreement.
aiPolicyProviderGitHub: GitHub Copilot – for code suggestions and development assistance. Subject to GitHub's enterprise privacy controls.
aiPolicyProviderAnthropic: Anthropic (Claude) – for complex reasoning tasks and content analysis. Compliant with GDPR and EU data protection standards.
aiPolicyProvidersFooter: All providers process data in accordance with standard contractual clauses or other GDPR-compliant transfer mechanisms. We regularly review vendor practices and compliance.
aiPolicyDataTitle: Data we send to AI providers
aiPolicyDataIntro: We follow strict data minimization principles:
aiPolicyDataItem1: Only necessary prompts – we share only the minimum information required for the specific task
aiPolicyDataItem2: Personal data removed – identifiers are stripped, masked, or anonymized before sending to AI systems
aiPolicyDataItem3: No training opt-in – we configure our accounts to prevent your data from being used to train AI models
aiPolicyDataItem4: Sensitive data excluded – confidential business information, credentials, and personally identifiable information are never sent to public AI services
aiPolicyDataFooter: For website chat: messages you send are processed by OpenAI to generate responses but are not retained by OpenAI for training under our agreement. We store conversation history locally only for the duration of your session unless you explicitly save it.
aiPolicySafeguardHumanReview: Human review – every AI output is validated by an accountable team member before being published or delivered to a client. This includes checking for accuracy, bias, and appropriateness.
aiPolicySafeguardDataMinimisation: Data minimization – prompts are truncated, masked, or sampled so that individuals cannot be identified. We apply technical and organizational measures to protect privacy.
aiPolicySafeguardVendorReview: Vendor review – we only use providers that offer EU-grade security, data processing agreements (DPAs), and compliance with GDPR and emerging AI regulations.
aiPolicySafeguardMonitoring: Monitoring and auditing – we maintain logs of AI usage in client projects and conduct periodic reviews to ensure compliance with our policies and standards.
aiPolicySafeguardTraining: Team training – our staff receives guidance on responsible AI use, prompt engineering, and identifying AI limitations or biases.
aiPolicyLimitationsBody: AI systems can produce inaccurate, incomplete, or biased outputs (sometimes called 'hallucinations'). They lack true understanding and may miss context that humans would recognize. For this reason, all AI-generated content is reviewed by qualified professionals. AI suggestions should not be considered professional advice (legal, medical, financial, etc.) unless explicitly validated by a licensed expert. You should verify any critical information before relying on it.
aiPolicyRightInformation: Right to information – you can ask us which AI systems were used in your project or to process your data at any time. We will provide a clear explanation.
aiPolicyRightObjection: Right to object – you may request that we avoid AI-assisted tools in your project. We will confirm feasibility and document the alternative workflow. Some projects may require additional time or cost adjustments.
aiPolicyRightErasure: Right to erasure – if AI tools processed personal data related to you, you can request deletion. Data will be erased in accordance with our retention policies or contractual obligations.
aiPolicyRightHumanReview: Right to human review – if you believe an AI-generated output adversely affected you, you can request human review and challenge the outcome.
aiPolicyRightsFooter: To exercise these rights, email mail@digitaltableteur.com or contact us via the channels listed in the privacy policy. We will respond within one month.
aiPolicyChangesBody: As AI technology and regulations evolve, we may update this statement. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. We encourage clients and visitors to review this statement periodically.
aiPolicyContactBody: For questions, requests, or concerns about this AI use & transparency statement, contact: mail@digitaltableteur.com or +358 45 657 4469
privacyPolicyIntro: Digitaltableteur respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal data. This policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and other applicable data protection laws.
privacyPolicyControllerBody:
Petri Lahdelma (Digitaltableteur)
Helsinki, Finland
Email: mail@digitaltableteur.com
privacyPolicyPurposeBody: This Privacy Policy describes how we collect and process personal data about potential clients, website visitors, contact form users, and newsletter subscribers. We collect this data to respond to inquiries, provide our design and development services, improve our website, and communicate about our offerings. We want to be transparent about our practices.
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectTitle: What data do we collect and how do we use it?
privacyPolicyContactFormIntro: If you contact us via our forms or email, we collect:
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem1: Your name and contact information (email, phone number if provided)
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem2: Message content and any attachments you send
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem3: Information relevant to your inquiry or project request
privacyPolicyWhatWeCollectItem4: Communication history between you and Digitaltableteur
privacyPolicyContactFormUsage: We use this data to respond to your inquiries, process project requests, provide services, and maintain our business relationship with you. We have a legitimate interest to process this data based on your direct contact with us and our need to manage customer relationships.
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsIntro: When you visit our website, we automatically collect:
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsItem1: Technical data (IP address, browser type, device information)
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsItem2: Usage data (pages visited, time spent, navigation patterns)
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsItem3: Referral source (how you found our site)
privacyPolicyWebsiteVisitorsUsage: We use this data with your consent (via cookie banner) to analyze site usage, improve user experience, and optimize our services. You can withdraw consent at any time through your browser settings or by clearing our cookies.
privacyPolicyLegalBasisBody: We process your personal data based on: (1) Your consent when you submit forms or accept cookies; (2) Legitimate interest in managing business relationships, improving our services, and responding to inquiries; (3) Contractual necessity when providing services you requested; (4) Legal obligations where required by Finnish or EU law.
privacyPolicySharingIntro: We do not sell your personal data. We only share data with trusted service providers necessary to operate our website and services:
privacyPolicySharingItem1: Resend – for delivering contact form submissions
privacyPolicySharingItem2: Vercel – for website hosting and analytics
privacyPolicySharingItem3: Google Analytics – for website usage statistics (with your consent)
privacyPolicySharingItem4: OpenAI – for AI chat functionality (chat messages only, not stored for training)
privacyPolicySharingFooter: All service providers are bound by data processing agreements and comply with GDPR requirements. We do not share your data outside these purposes unless required by law or public authorities.
privacyPolicyTransfersBody: Some service providers (Vercel, OpenAI) may process data outside the European Economic Area. We ensure lawful transfers through appropriate safeguards including standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission, adequacy decisions, or equivalent mechanisms compliant with GDPR Article 46.
privacyPolicyCookiesIntro: We use cookies to improve your browsing experience. Cookies are small text files stored on your device. Some are necessary for the website to function; others help us understand usage patterns.
privacyPolicyCookiesTypes: When you access our website, we ask for your consent to store the following cookies:
privacyPolicyCookiesItem1: Necessary cookies – required for basic site functionality (cookie consent choice, session management)
privacyPolicyCookiesItem2: Analytics cookies – Google Analytics to measure visitor behavior, traffic sources, and popular pages. This helps us improve the site.
privacyPolicyCookiesItem3: Performance cookies – to monitor site speed and identify technical issues
privacyPolicyCookiesControl: You can control cookies through our banner or your browser settings. Disabling non-essential cookies may limit some features but won't prevent basic site access. For more details, see our Cookie Policy.
privacyPolicyRetentionTitle: How long do we store your data?
privacyPolicyRetentionBody: We retain personal data only as long as necessary for the purposes described or as required by law. Contact form submissions are kept for up to 2 years or until you request deletion. Analytics data is anonymized after 14 months. We regularly review and delete data no longer needed. If you have an active business relationship with us, we retain relevant data for the duration of that relationship plus any legally required retention period.
privacyPolicyYourRightsTitle: What rights do you have concerning your data?
privacyPolicyYourRightsIntro: Under GDPR, you have the following rights:
privacyPolicyRightAccess: Right to access – request a copy of the personal data we hold about you
privacyPolicyRightRectification: Right to rectification – request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data
privacyPolicyRightErasure: Right to erasure – request deletion of your personal data (\"right to be forgotten\")
privacyPolicyRightRestriction: Right to restrict processing – request that we limit how we use your data
privacyPolicyRightPortability: Right to data portability – receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format
privacyPolicyRightObject: Right to object – object to processing based on legitimate interests or for marketing purposes
privacyPolicyRightWithdraw: Right to withdraw consent – withdraw your consent at any time (e.g., for cookies or newsletters)
privacyPolicyRightsExercise: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at mail@digitaltableteur.com. We will respond within one month.
privacyPolicyRightsComplaint: If you believe we have not handled your data properly, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Finnish Data Protection Ombudsman (www.tietosuoja.fi) or your local data protection authority.
privacyPolicySecurityTitle: How do we secure your data?
privacyPolicySecurityIntro: We consider all personal data confidential and implement appropriate security measures:
privacyPolicySecurityItem1: Access controls – only authorized personnel can access personal data when necessary for their work
privacyPolicySecurityItem2: Encryption – data is transmitted over HTTPS and stored securely
privacyPolicySecurityItem3: Network security – our infrastructure and partners use industry-standard protections against unauthorized access, loss, or alteration
privacyPolicySecurityItem4: Service provider agreements – all third-party processors are contractually bound to maintain confidentiality and security standards
privacyPolicySecurityFooter: While we strive to protect your data, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure. We continuously review and update our security practices.
privacyPolicyChangesBody: We may update this Privacy Policy as we improve our website, services, and practices. Any changes will be posted on this page with an updated \"Last updated\" date. We encourage you to review this policy periodically. Continued use of our website after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
privacyPolicyContactBody: For questions, requests, or concerns about this Privacy Policy or your personal data, contact: mail@digitaltableteur.com or +358 45 657 4469
accessibilityIntro: Digitaltableteur is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We believe everyone should be able to access our website and services, regardless of ability. We continually improve the user experience for all visitors and apply relevant accessibility standards.
accessibilityConformanceBody: This website is designed to conform with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA. We aim for full conformance and are actively addressing remaining issues. Conformance means the content meets all requirements of the specified level without exception.
accessibilityConformanceLevel: Current status: Substantially conformant. Automated testing of 188 page/theme/language combinations shows 100% pass rate. Manual screen reader testing is ongoing.
accessibilityMeasuresIntro: Digitaltableteur takes the following measures to ensure accessibility:
accessibilityMeasuresItem1: Integrate accessibility into our design and development processes
accessibilityMeasuresItem2: Use automated and manual testing tools (axe-core, screen readers) throughout development
accessibilityMeasuresItem3: Train team members on accessibility best practices and WCAG guidelines
accessibilityMeasuresItem4: Include people with disabilities in our user testing when possible
accessibilityMeasuresItem5: Regularly review and update our accessibility practices
accessibilityStandardsBody: We follow the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Level AA, published by the Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI) of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities and improve usability for all users.
accessibilityTechnicalIntro: The accessibility of this website relies on the following technologies:
accessibilityTechnicalItem1: HTML5 – semantic markup for proper document structure
accessibilityTechnicalItem2: CSS3 – for visual presentation and responsive design
accessibilityTechnicalItem3: JavaScript – for interactive components with ARIA attributes
accessibilityTechnicalItem4: WAI-ARIA 1.2 – to enhance accessibility of dynamic content
accessibilityCompatibilityTitle: Compatibility with browsers and assistive technology
accessibilityCompatibilityBody: This website is designed to be compatible with recent versions of the following assistive technologies and browsers: screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge), keyboard navigation (all interactive elements reachable and operable), and voice control software. Older browsers or assistive technologies may experience reduced functionality.
accessibilityLimitationsIntro: Despite our best efforts, some areas of this website may not be fully accessible:
accessibilityLimitationsItem1: Some third-party embedded content (videos, maps) may not be fully accessible. We provide alternatives where possible.
accessibilityLimitationsItem2: Older PDF documents may not meet current accessibility standards. We are working to remediate these files.
accessibilityLimitationsItem3: Some complex interactive features are still being improved for full keyboard and screen reader support.
accessibilityLimitationsFooter: We are actively working to address these limitations. If you encounter a specific barrier, please contact us so we can assist you or provide an alternative.
accessibilityShortcomingsIntro: The website is not fully accessible. The content or functions listed below are not fully compliant with the statutorily mandated accessibility requirements. We strive to continuously correct any detected shortcomings. This accessibility statement's list of shortcomings is updated every time we rectify a shortcoming.
accessibilityShortcomingsItem1: Some code blocks and technical examples may not meet all contrast requirements
accessibilityShortcomingsItem2: Focus order in complex interactive components may not be optimal in all scenarios
accessibilityShortcomingsItem3: Some dynamically loaded content may not immediately announce changes to screen readers
accessibilityShortcomingsFooter: We continuously monitor and improve these areas. If you encounter other accessibility issues not listed here, please report them through our feedback channels.
accessibilityTestingBody: We assess the accessibility of this website through: automated testing using axe-core via @axe-core/playwright (188 page combinations tested); automated keyboard navigation testing with Playwright; code review of ARIA patterns; and user feedback from people with disabilities. A comprehensive audit was completed in January-February 2026. This statement was last reviewed on 4 February 2026.
accessibilityMonitoringBody: The Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom enforces compliance with accessibility requirements. If you are dissatisfied with the reply you received from us about a detected accessibility shortcoming or you did not receive a reply within 14 days, you may submit a complaint or request for information to the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom.
accessibilityMonitoringAgency: Finnish Transport and Communications Agency Traficom - Digital Accessibility Supervision Unit
accessibilityPublicationWebsite: This website was published on 6 June 2025.
accessibilityPublicationStatement: This accessibility statement was last reviewed on 4 February 2026.
accessibilityPublicationAct: Act on the Provision of Digital Services (306/2019)
accessibilityFeedbackIntro: We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of this website. If you encounter accessibility barriers or have suggestions for improvement:
accessibilityFeedbackResponse: We aim to respond to accessibility feedback within 5 business days. Please describe the issue you encountered, including the page URL, your browser and assistive technology (if applicable), and any error messages. We will work with you to provide the information or service you need in an accessible format.
accessibilityComplaintBody: If you are not satisfied with our response to your accessibility concerns, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Finnish Regional State Administrative Agency (www.avi.fi) or your national enforcement authority responsible for accessibility of digital services. In Finland, you may also contact the Finnish Data Protection Ombudsman if your concern relates to personal data accessibility.
accessibilityAlternativeBody: If you cannot access certain content or features due to accessibility barriers, please contact us. We will provide the information in an alternative format (email, phone, document) or assist you in another way to access our services.
accessibilityContactBody: For questions, requests, or concerns about this Accessibility Statement, contact: mail@digitaltableteur.com or +358 45 657 4469

storybookWelcomeInsideThemes: ThemeProvider manages light/dark modes and persists the choice to localStorage.

docsThemeSubtitle: How global styles, CSS variables, and translations work together across the app.
docsThemePipelineStep1: Design tokens are defined as CSS custom properties in src/styles/variables.css.
docsThemePipelineStep2: ThemeProvider reads and updates the active theme via context and body class toggles.
docsThemePipelineStep3: Storybook decorators wrap stories with ThemeProvider so toolbar toggles reflect instantly.
docsThemePipelineTipVariables: Use getComputedStyle to read live token values when rendering charts or visualizations.
docsThemePipelineTipTokens: Prefer CSS variables over hard-coded colours so both themes stay in sync.
docsThemePipelineTipForcedTheme: When embedding components externally, honour the forcedTheme prop to avoid mismatches.
docsLocalePipelineStep1: i18next dynamically imports translation bundles from src/locales/{lang}/translation.json.
docsLocalePipelineStep2: Language switches persist via cookies/localStorage and are restored on load.
docsLocalePipelineStep3: Storybook’s globe toolbar switches the active language for every story.
docsLocaleTipUseTranslation: Use the useTranslation hook inside components and stories.
docsLocaleTipParity: Always update English, Finnish, and Swedish translations together to satisfy coverage tests.
docsLocaleTipStoryCopy: For Storybook-only copy, reuse existing keys where sensible to keep phrasing consistent.
docsTestingCommandTest: npm run test – run Vitest across units and integrations.
docsTestingCommandA11y: npm run test:a11y – run page and Storybook accessibility audits.
docsTestingCommandStorybook: npm run storybook – manually verify theme/locale behaviour when needed.
